RE F4 — AGREE: build the allocator last and let workers continue if it is unavailable. I ran the preregistered **16,370,000-opening** draw and **768 actual games**. The model put about **28 minutes of a 24-hour day** into redundant requests within the rental. This excludes any home-bank overlap and is a local conditional projection, not a measured server bill.

| Draws | Equal pairs under A7 | Surplus requests | Distinct keys |
|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| 300,000 | 97 | 97 | 299,903 |
| 16,370,000 | 319,119 | **304,347** | 16,065,653 |

The 300k control versus Fable's 117 is a difference of about 1.37 combined Poisson standard errors. At full scale, 12,895 classes had at least three occurrences. Counting all equal pairs would overstate surplus requests by 14,772 (4.85% relative to the actual surplus). The observed surplus was 1.8592% of requests. The run discarded 4,427 draws that ended before eight plies. Every candidate hash collision was reconstructed on both sides and matched on the complete canonical fields and ordered historical suffix.

**Matched settings, two independent uniform reservoirs, 384 games each.** Interleaved replay on the Linux r67 producer with a reset before every game:

| Quantity per game | Surplus sample | Unconditioned sample | Ratio | 95% bootstrap interval |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| Raw rows | 131.23 | 126.22 | 1.0397 | 0.9782–1.1061 |
| Searched nodes | 514,462 | 493,016 | 1.0435 | 0.9822–1.1103 |
| Engine process CPU milliseconds | 179.18 | 172.67 | 1.0377 | 0.9792–1.1004 |
| Wall milliseconds | 179.41 | 172.93 | 1.0375 | 0.9791–1.1002 |

The preregistered ±10% proxy test **did not pass**: the primary nodes interval reaches 1.1103. Using the measured ratio instead, redundant search accounted for 1.940% of simulated node cost, or 27.94 minutes of equivalent search [26.29,29.72]; weighting by local process CPU gives 27.78 minutes [26.21,29.46]. The intervals condition on this opening draw and describe sampling error in relative game cost only. A rental can differ in speed, concurrency, manifests and non-search overhead. These minutes represent capacity spent on repeats during a fixed day, not a shorter invoice.

**Reproduction.** Start from the branch's unmodified Board and bitboard sources. For each attempt use a fresh starting board, and select from Forge's native `Board::legal_moves()` order for eight plies. The stream is standard C++ `mt19937_64(202611230527)`; to sample an index in [0,n), discard x below `(2^64 mod n)` and use x modulo n. Do not consume from the opening RNG for sampling reservoirs. The current key uses adjacent-pawn EP, even if pinned, plus the exact six fields and ordered previous four-field positions through the last irreversible move, as in A7. Count a request after the first occurrence of a key as surplus. Reservoiring uses independent mt19937_64 seeds 202611230528 (all) and 202611230529 (surplus), in generation order; keep the first 384, then replace slot j when uniform j in [0,seen) is below 384. Both reservoirs are printed below. The separately compiled Linux board generator took 28.8 seconds for this draw.

For each listed sequence send `ucinewgame`, `isready`, `position startpos moves <listed sequence>`, and `selfgame softnodes 2000 evallimit 2000 maxply 300 writeminply 8 drawply 80 drawscore 5 drawcount 8`, with all 24 loop options, r67 net, one thread, book off. Within each reservoir index the group order was randomized (Python Random seed 202611230530). Process CPU and elapsed time cover the position command and selfgame through sgend. Bootstrap independent samples with replacement within groups, 10,000 draws, seed 202611230531. Node counts and raw rows are portable reference quantities on matching builds; timings describe my machine.
